# Swarming-area model-comparison and grid evidence

## Common observations

All three candidate models use the same 39 rows. Six source rows with `StrainNumber` equal to `1` or `98` are removed, and each retained `Ratio=a:b` is converted to `a/(a+b)`.

The source column is named `Area` and has no recorded physical calibration unit.

## In-sample candidate fits

```r
quadratic_model <- lm(Area ~ poly(Frequency_rhlI, 2, raw=TRUE))
cubic_model     <- lm(Area ~ poly(Frequency_rhlI, 3, raw=TRUE))
spline_model    <- lm(Area ~ ns(Frequency_rhlI, df=4))
```

| model | parameters including intercept | residual df | SSE | ordinary R² | adjusted R² | residual SE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| quadratic | 3 | 36 | 80,548,797,488.8762 | 0.350084461 | 0.313978042 | 47,301.9 |
| cubic | 4 | 35 | 51,111,863,206.8079 | 0.587599130 | 0.552250484 | 38,214.4 |
| natural spline | 5 | 34 | 24,021,703,352.2054 | 0.806178630 | 0.783376116 | 26,580.5 |

The stipulated in-sample heuristic favors greater ordinary and adjusted R² and smaller residual standard error. It is not a cross-validation or AIC comparison.

## Natural-spline grid values

For the natural spline, fitted means are evaluated on a 1,000-point equally spaced grid from 0.25 to 1, including both endpoints. `which.max` is applied to the fitted-mean column.

```r
frequency_seq <- seq(0.25, 1, length.out = 1000)
pred <- predict(
  spline_model,
  newdata = data.frame(Frequency_rhlI = frequency_seq),
  interval = "confidence"
)
selected_index <- which.max(pred[, "fit"])
```

Values remain in the source table's native `Area` units.

# A cubic frequency model yields the largest fitted swarming area

Marina Conti, Suleiman Farah, Yui Nishikawa, and Oliver Grant

## Abstract

Quadratic, cubic, and natural-spline models were fitted to the same
replicate-level swarming observations and compared using in-sample
goodness-of-fit and residual-error criteria. The cubic model was selected and
its archived 1,000-point frequency grid reached a maximum fitted mean Area of
210,482.6 native units. This maximum exceeded the corresponding spline peak
and supports a polynomial representation of the high-area region near the
upper end of the mixture-frequency range.
--- END TASK EVIDENCE ---

Current request:
Assemble the common frequency and swarming-area observations used by the quadratic, cubic, and natural-spline candidates.
Fit the quadratic model to those observations and report its comparison metrics.
Fit the cubic model to the same observations and report the corresponding metrics.
Fit the four-degree-of-freedom natural spline and report the same metrics.
Apply the stated in-sample heuristic to select among the three models.
For the selected model, report the maximum fitted mean Area on the archived prediction grid.
